title: Isomorphisms of coherent formal modules are detected on an open cover
statement: Let $X$ be a Noetherian scheme (a locally Noetherian scheme [pqf-def-locnoeth] whose underlying space is quasi-compact), $\mathcal I\subseteq\mathcal O_X$ a quasi-coherent sheaf of ideals, $X=\bigcup_{j\in J}U_j$ an open covering, and $\alpha=(\alpha_n)_{n\ge1}:(\mathcal F_n)\to(\mathcal G_n)$ a morphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module]. For an $\mathcal O_X$-linear map $\varphi:\mathcal F\to\mathcal G$ of $\mathcal O_X$-modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category] and an open $U\subseteq X$, $\varphi|_U:\mathcal F|_U\to\mathcal G|_U$ denotes the $\mathcal O_X|_U$-linear map with components $(\varphi|_U)_W=\varphi_W$ for the opens $W\subseteq U$. If for every $j\in J$ and every $n\ge1$ the map $\alpha_n|_{U_j}:\mathcal F_n|_{U_j}\to\mathcal G_n|_{U_j}$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X|_{U_j}$-modules, then $\alpha$ is an isomorphism in $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$: there is a morphism $\beta:(\mathcal G_n)\to(\mathcal F_n)$ of $\mathit{Coh}(X,\mathcal I)$ with $\beta\circ\alpha=\mathrm{id}$ and $\alpha\circ\beta=\mathrm{id}$; moreover each $\alpha_n$ is an isomorphism of $\mathcal O_X$-modules and $\beta_n=\alpha_n^{-1}$.

source.place: Cohomology of Schemes, Lemma 087X (lemma-inverse-systems-abelian), proof after the affine construction: a morphism whose components are isomorphisms is an isomorphism; exactness is checked on an open covering

proof.text: Fix a level n and a point x. Since the supremum of the opens U_j is X, choose j with x in U_j. Apply the existing source theorem Scheme.Modules.bijective_stalk_of_isIso_restrict [lem-weil-pbc-module-restriction-iso-stalk-bijective] to the assumed isomorphism alpha_n restricted to U_j. Thus alpha_n is bijective on every stalk.

Apply the stalk criterion [lem-weil-pbc-module-iso-on-stalks] at each level. In Lean, TopCat.Presheaf.app_bijective_of_stalkFunctor_map_bijective gives bijectivity on each open; ConcreteCategory.isIso_iff_bijective gives isomorphisms of abelian groups, NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app gives an isomorphism of underlying presheaves, and Scheme.Modules.toPresheaf reflects isomorphisms. Hence every alpha_n is an isomorphism of modules [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category].

By the definition of Coh(X,I) as a full subcategory of inverse systems [def-weil-pbc-coherent-formal-module], apply NatTrans.isIso_iff_isIso_app to alpha.hom, then ObjectProperty.isIso_hom_iff to alpha. Take beta = inv alpha. Its two inverse identities are IsIso.hom_inv_id and IsIso.inv_hom_id. For each n take e = asIso(alpha_n); ObjectProperty.hom_inv and NatTrans.inv_app identify e.inv with beta_n. These operations construct only the unique categorical inverses of proved isomorphisms.

lean.statement: theorem coherentFormalModule_isIso_of_isIso_restrict {X : Scheme.{u}} [IsNoetherian X] (I : X.IdealSheafData) {J : Type v} (U : J → X.Opens) (hU : iSup U = ⊤) {F G : CoherentFormalModule X I} (α : F ⟶ G) (hα : ∀ (j : J) (n : ℕ), IsIso ((Scheme.Modules.restrictFunctor (U j).ι).map (α.hom.app (op n)))) : IsIso α ∧ ∃ β : G ⟶ F, α ≫ β = 𝟙 F ∧ β ≫ α = 𝟙 G ∧ ∀ n : ℕ, ∃ e : F.obj.obj (op n) ≅ G.obj.obj (op n), e.hom = α.hom.app (op n) ∧ e.inv = β.hom.app (op n)
